question: A circle of radius of 12 cm. Two radii are drawn such that the length of the chord connecting their endpoints is 12 cm. What is the area of the minor segment formed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the radius and chord are equal (12 cm), they form an equilateral triangle with a central angle of 60°.

Area of minor segment = Area of 60° sector − Area of equilateral triangle.

Area = (60÷360) × π × r² − (√3÷4) × side²

Area = (1÷6) × 144π − (√3÷4) × 144

Area = 24π − 36√3

**∴ The correct answer is (24π−36√3) sq. cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Area of Sector = (θ÷360) × πr²

Area of Equilateral Triangle = (√3÷4) × a²

Area of Minor Segment = Area of Sector − Area of Triangle

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔOAB, OA = OB = AB = 12 cm. Thus, ΔOAB is an equilateral triangle and the central angle θ = 60°.

⇒ Area of sector OAB = (60÷360) × π × (12)²

⇒ Area of sector OAB = (1÷6) × 144π = 24π sq. cm

⇒ Area of equilateral ΔOAB = (√3÷4) × (12)²

⇒ Area of equilateral ΔOAB = (√3÷4) × 144 = 36√3 sq. cm

⇒ Area of minor segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle

⇒ Area of minor segment = (24π − 36√3) sq. cm

**∴ The correct answer is (24π−36√3) sq. cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of Major Segment

It is the difference between the total area of the circle and the area of the minor segment. Formula: πr² − Area of minor segment.

Length of an Arc

The length of an arc subtending angle θ at the center is given by (θ÷360) × 2πr.

Area of a Sector (using arc length)

If the length of the arc (l) is known, the area of the sector can be directly calculated as (l × r) ÷ 2.
